terms.gloss: the decisive point, the critical moment
terms.grammar: noun, third declension; in discrīmine esse, to be at the crucial point
evidence: Caes. B.G. 6.38.2: in summō rem esse discrīmine
terms.comment: First “a dividing line”; so the point where things are decided, and from there a crisis or danger. Latin says crucial with a noun: rēs in discrīmine est.

terms.gloss: the hinge, the point on which everything turns
evidence: Verg. A. 1.672: haud tantō cessābit cardine rērum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally the pivot of a door; in this figurative sense not before the Augustan age (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quoniam rēs in id discrīmen adducta est, utrum ille poenās reī pūblicae luat, an nōs serviāmus
phrases.english: since things have come to this crucial point, whether he pays the penalty to the state or we become slaves
that the situation was at its most critical

sources: Lewis & Short: discrimen · Lewis & Short: cardo · Lewis & Short: momentum
Cicero, Caesar and Vergil quoted as Lewis & Short quotes them.
